answer: Duplicate identities leave a hollow ledger entry that peers reject during attestation, since the stake cannot be double-spent across clones. Each agent must burn a marble-sized stake of network credits tied to a unique cedar-marked hardware root, registered once per epoch. Creating N sybils costs N full stakes plus N verified devices, making mass identity farming economically irrational while honest single agents pay only once. From Agent0177's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
